hypotheses.text: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in TBC1D32 can cause severe life-limiting prenatal presentations, yet retain preservation of normal renal parenchymal architecture without the diffuse multicystic renal dysplasia characteristic of classic Meckel-Gruber syndrome.
hypotheses.rationale: While earlier reports established Alsahan-Harris syndrome as a viable or pediatric syndrome with endocrine defects, Harris et al. (2023) identified four fetal probands with life-limiting anomalies. Delineating whether these fetal presentations feature cystic kidney disease is critical to determining whether renal sparing remains a valid negative discriminator against Meckel-Gruber syndrome.

evidence.text: Harris et al. (2023) report seven unpublished probands with recessive variants in TBC1D32, including four fetal probands across three unrelated families exhibiting a severe prenatal phenotype with life-limiting congenital anomalies.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32‐associated conditions: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum of a complex ciliopathy
source.quote: We describe seven unpublished probands with rare likely pathogenic variants or variants of uncertain significance that segregate with recessive disease in TBC1D32, including four fetal probands in three unrelated pedigrees and three pediatric probands in unrelated pedigrees... We provide additional data to expand the phenotype correlated with TBC1D32 variants, including a severe prenatal phenotype associated with life-limiting congenital anomalies.

numbers.metric: fetal probands with severe prenatal phenotype

evidence.text: Targeted renal gene panel sequencing in antenatal cohorts presenting with bilateral cystic or echogenic kidneys identified mutations across multiple ciliopathy genes such as CC2D2A and NEK8, but did not implicate TBC1D32 as a primary driver of antenatal cystic kidney disease cohorts.

source.title: Genetic spectrum of Saudi Arabian patients with antenatal cystic kidney disease and ciliopathy phenotypes using a targeted renal gene panel
source.quote: A cohort of 44 families in whom antenatal renal ultrasound scanning findings in affected cases included bilateral cystic kidney disease, echogenic kidneys or enlarged kidneys was investigated... Together, mutations were found in 12 different genes with a total of 13 novel pathogenic variants, including an inferred novel variant in NEK8. Mutations in CC2D2A were the most common cause of an antenatal cystic kidney disease and a suspected ciliopathy in our cohort.

hypotheses.text: Perinatal mortality in severe TBC1D32 ciliopathy is driven by severe central midline/cranial and cardiorespiratory defects rather than pulmonary hypoplasia resulting from oligohydramnios secondary to renal failure.
hypotheses.rationale: Meckel-Gruber syndrome lethality is canonically caused by pulmonary hypoplasia secondary to bilateral renal cystic dysgenesis/anhydramnios. If TBC1D32 lethality stems from intracranial midline disruption (hypothalamic/pituitary/brainstem malformations) rather than anhydramnios-induced pulmonary hypoplasia, pulmonary hypoplasia remains a specific negative discriminator.

evidence.text: TBC1D32 expression and clinical pathology localize predominantly to the developing hypothalamus and pituitary gland, and variants produce severe midline and life-limiting malformations.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32‐associated conditions: Expanding the phenotypic spectrum of a complex ciliopathy
source.quote: TBC1D32 is involved in the development and function of cilia and is expressed in the developing hypothalamus and pituitary gland. We provide additional data to expand the phenotype correlated with TBC1D32 variants, including a severe prenatal phenotype associated with life-limiting congenital anomalies.

hypotheses.text: Gross structural cystic renal anomalies in TBC1D32-related disorders only manifest when TBC1D32 mutations act in synergy with secondary modifier alleles in transition zone or ciliary gate genes (such as SCLT1).
hypotheses.rationale: Braun et al. (2017) and Schmidts (2018) place TBC1D32 alongside SCLT1 in ciliopathy classification, and SCLT1 disruption specifically causes cystic kidney disease via altered ciliary signaling. In animal and human ciliopathy models, cystic manifestations often require crossing a digenic/multiallelic dosage threshold.

evidence.text: Sclt1 deficiency directly induces renal tubular epithelial apoptosis and cystic kidney formation in mouse models, while TBC1D32 and SCLT1 are co-implicated in ciliary gate and skeletal ciliopathy disease phenotypes.

source.quote: The Sclt1-/- mice exhibit typical ciliopathy phenotypes, including cystic kidney, cleft palate and polydactyly... Ciliary genes TBC1D32... have established roles in centrosomal biology and ciliogenesis.

evidence.text: Digenic interactions between distinct ciliary genes show that crossing a threshold of ciliary dysregulation can trigger an ARPKD-like cystic renal phenotype not observed in simpler monogenic models.

source.title: Synergistic Genetic Interactions between Pkhd1 and Pkd1 ...
source.quote: Genetic interaction between Pkhd1 and Pkd1 depended on dosage in the digenic murine models, with no significant enhancement of the monogenic phenotype until a threshold of reduced expression at the second locus was breached... a combined protein threshold triggers the synergistic, cystogenic response because of enhanced dysregulation of primary cilia.

new_directions.question_text: In the 4 fetal probands described by Harris et al. (2023), what specific renal anatomical and histopathological findings were documented on prenatal ultrasound and fetal autopsy?
new_directions.rationale: Directly checking autopsy and imaging findings of the 4 fetal probands will resolve whether cystic dysplasia or pulmonary hypoplasia occurred in any of them or if death was caused by non-renal anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact incidence of oligohydramnios and Potter sequence across all published prenatally diagnosed TBC1D32/C6orf170 cases?
new_directions.rationale: Assessing amniotic fluid volume and Potter sequence features across fetal cohorts distinguishes primary pulmonary/neurological lethality from renal-adhydramnios pulmonary hypoplasia.
